  Incremental reconstruction regression fixtures

  These are small synthetic HEVC fixtures preserved from the incremental
  decoding experiment. Direct, tall, grid, pipeline, and transformed versions
  exercise row lifetime and pixel mapping. The HEIC and golden files below
  are the exact bytes used for the comparisons.

  Golden PNGs were generated as RGBA8 using strict primary-image decoding
  from libheif 1.21.2, commit 78638f4fe417e49f2b129f42ae691a4954560bbd,
  backed by libde265 1.1.1. No decoding warnings were returned.

  odd-single-grid.png uses the same source with libheif-border-index.patch
  applied. In the 4:2:0 bilinear upsampling border loops, cx and cy already
  count chroma samples, so dividing them by two again reads the wrong
  positions. The patch corrects only those indices. The original oracle
  disagrees with this fixture by up to 255 at the outer border; all samples
  differing by more than one lie on that border. The corrected oracle and
  incremental decoder agree within one. This exception is local to a pinned
  fixture, not a global relaxation or an upstream-confirmed fix.

  Other fixture PNGs use the original unmodified oracle. They have no ICC
  profile, and their alpha is opaque. Allocation tests compare these golden
  images through an independent area average. Cases without a PNG compare
  to the existing Rust full decoder plus independent area averaging.

Review regression fixtures

odd-width-grid derives from odd-single-grid by setting the visible grid
width to 255 and clean-aperture width to 253. Its paired 256-wide canvas
with a horizontal aperture offset of -1/2 produces the identical strict
oracle PNG. The retained aperture excludes the original canvas borders.

odd-height-grid uses the same tile decoded by FFmpeg 9.0.1, rotated
clockwise, and encoded with libx265 lossless=1:keyint=1:wpp=0:
repeat-headers=1:pools=none as yuv420p. It has a 256x255 grid canvas and
centered 254x253 aperture. A 256-high control with vertical aperture
offset -1/2 produces the identical strict oracle PNG. The PPS enables
transquant bypass; decoded SAO components are zero.

undefined-grid-nclx derives from grid.heic with nclx 1/13/1, limited range,
associated to all tiles and nclx 2/2/2, full range, on the primary. A
control omitting only the primary association produces the same PNG.

All three new PNGs use the original strict pinned libheif oracle above,
without the border patch, and return zero warnings.

grid-pipeline repeats pipeline.heic's HEVC tile in a 2x2 grid using
scripts/incremental/wrap.rb. Each tile is 1024x1088; the visible canvas is
2048x2176. Strict live-oracle comparisons pass at max_side 6000 and 65.

invalid-grid-references.bin is deliberately malformed. It derives from
grid.heic by replacing its four dimg targets with 65,535 references to
tile 1, updating box lengths and iloc offsets, while retaining the 2x2
descriptor. Allocation tests require tile-count rejection within 256 KiB
for both Path and Bytes. It is excluded from positive *.heic comparisons.
